name: Grain Swap — Live Viability-Driven Switch
description: Fig 5 as a fully runnable temporal study: a cell's viability is driven down by a simple external stress ramp (StressRamp), and a GrainSelector swaps which grain realizes the shared interface as a function of that viability. While viability >= 0.5 the cheap CoarseGrainProcess (linear yield) produces the interface's biomass; once viability slides below 0.5 control switches to the mechanistic FineGrainProcess (saturating Michaelis-Menten), which resolves the regime near the boundary. Exactly one grain is active per tick, so the coarse->fine handover happens on-screen as viability crosses the threshold. This is the demonstration behind Fig 5b: a process is swapped between grains on the viability function. Runnable (default_n_steps + RAMEmitter).
